correctness.rationale: The greedy-block criterion is necessary and sufficient for embeddings in both ordered block strings. Inserting between equal neighbors preserves each budget; two-sided and one-sided insertion lemmas fill all remaining budgets, proving maximal implies length 2m−1. The one-sided argument uses a precise minimal/maximum endpoint and forbidden-split contradiction, not an unproved counting heuristic. The ternary rational matrix and constant-term expression reproduce the binomial formula; independent exhaustive tests cover 15 input cells and DP comparisons cover 40 ternary repetitions. Boundary q=2 and m=1 are included. Finite tests are corroboration, not a proof of all parameters.

evidence: A maximal common subsequence is insertion-maximal, whereas longest is cardinality-maximal; these are generally distinct.
The new claim equates the two notions on a specific two-string periodic family and converts the admissible words to balanced walks.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Equivalent searches used the terms inclusion-maximal, length-maximal, reversing permutations, balanced ascent/descent walks, and repeated blocks. value.rationale: The exact infinite-family classification resolves the otherwise nontrivial distinction between inclusion-maximal and cardinality-maximal common subsequences. The closed ternary formula and asymptotic give a precise exponentially growing output benchmark for enumeration of an algorithmically motivated object; unlike a small finite census this gives all repetition counts and alphabet sizes structurally.
